6. **Avoid premature optimization** - Clarity first, optimize measured problems
7. **Use value receivers for small structs** - Avoid pointer indirection

content.value_statement: Go services can become slow or memory-heavy without clear evidence. This skill guides profiling, allocation analysis, concurrency tuning, and benchmark-driven optimization.
actual_capabilities: Explains CPU, heap, and allocation profiling with pprof endpoints and local commands.
Shows programmatic CPU and memory profile collection using Go runtime packages.
Describes allocation reduction using preallocated slices, builders, copies, and sync.Pool.
Covers escape analysis commands and examples that identify heap allocations.
Demonstrates worker pools, buffered channels, lock sharding, and sync.Map tradeoffs.
Provides benchmark patterns for timing, allocation reports, and implementation comparisons.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not run benchmarks by itself.
Recommendations must be validated against your workload and production profile data.
Examples assume standard Go tooling and access to the target project.
It does not cover every runtime flag, trace workflow, or third-party profiler.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Slow API Paths
use_cases.description: Plan CPU and memory profiling for Go services with latency or throughput issues.

use_cases.title: Reduce Memory Pressure
use_cases.description: Identify allocation-heavy code paths and choose practical changes that reduce garbage collection pressure.

use_cases.title: Review Optimization Proposals
use_cases.description: Evaluate concurrency, data structure, and benchmark changes before merging performance work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a profiling plan for my Go service. Focus on CPU, heap, and allocation data to collect first.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Allocations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Go function for avoidable allocations. Suggest changes that preserve readability and explain how to benchmark them.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Concurrency
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my worker pool and locking strategy for contention risks. Recommend measurements and safer concurrency improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Benchmarks
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these Go benchmark results and profile observations. Identify the likely bottleneck and propose the next experiment.

output_examples.input: A Go API has high CPU usage during request bursts.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a profiling plan, key pprof views to inspect, likely hot-path questions, and remeasurement steps.

output_examples.input: A batch job allocates large amounts of memory while processing strings.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests allocation checks, builder or buffer reuse options, and benchmark measurements for before and after results.

output_examples.input: A team wants to review a proposed worker pool change.
output_examples.output: The skill highlights channel sizing, lock contention, backpressure, and benchmark evidence needed before approval.

best_practices: Measure with profiles and benchmarks before changing performance-sensitive code.
Optimize one bottleneck at a time, then remeasure with the same workload.
Keep profiling endpoints local or access controlled when used outside development.
anti_patterns: Optimizing code based only on intuition or style preferences.
Applying every optimization pattern without workload evidence.
Comparing benchmark runs from different machines, loads, or compiler settings.

faq.question: Does this skill run Go commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples. Commands run only when the user or agent chooses to execute them.

faq.question: Can it fix performance problems without profile data?
faq.answer: It can suggest likely checks, but profile and benchmark data are needed for reliable optimization decisions.

faq.question: Does it support pprof workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers CPU, heap, allocation, and programmatic profiling patterns using pprof.

faq.question: Can it help with memory leaks?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains allocation profiles, slice retention issues, object reuse, and garbage collection pressure.

faq.question: Is it only for production systems?
faq.answer: No. It can help during development, testing, staging, and production investigations.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
